Article Title: 'Prioritise national interest': Shashi Tharoor advises govt to keep Brics 'non-West'
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti-West.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday cautioned that the Brics summit hosted by India should not appear to be an anti-West platform, as that would not be in sync with the country’s national interests.Tharoor, who served as a diplomat at the United Nations for decades, advised the government to showcase the concerns of the Global South while keeping India’s direct national interests in mind."As chair, we have a particular responsibility to showcase both the Brics as a forum, the concerns of the Global South in general, but also while bearing very, very carefully in mind our direct national interests. We want Brics to be a forum that is non-West, but not anti-West. That is exactly actually the same agenda as every other country. There are some others in Brics who are very happy to take it as a geopolitical non-Western, but also anti-Western platform," Tharoor told news agency PTI.He also said that PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"."And I would like to say that that would not be in India's national interest...Becauseall these world leaders are in India, there will be significant bilateral conversations. Our Prime Minister is bound to be meeting each of the visiting heads of state and government who seeks a meeting. And that may mean a dozen important meetings with these country leaders. And for us, of course, both the meeting with President Xi and the meeting with President Putin are going to grab world headlines," the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP said.Former Union minister Salman Khurshid also described the gathering as a “significant event” that allows India to demonstrate leadership on the global stage.Speaking to ANI, Khurshid stressed that the presence of leaders from all 11 member countries, including China, Iran, Russia, South Africa and India, could help New Delhi bring countries together, reduce contradictions and conflicts, and work towards creating better conditions in the world."This is a significant event. We hosted the G20 summit a few years ago, and the important thing is that the top leadership of China, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and India will all be present. All 11 countries will be present. It allows India to demonstrate leadership and ensure that contradictions and conflicts are reduced to a minimum. It can't be done overnight, but at least some attempt should be made. For India to have a locus as the leader and chairperson of the Brics summit, to be able to bring people together, converge, and accept positions that will create better conditions in the world," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said leaders from across the world would gather in New Delhi over the next few days for the Brics summit, expressing confidence that the high-level meeting would see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind.“Over the next few days, leaders from around the world will gather for the Brics Summit. I am confident that the Summit will see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind,” Modi said in a post on X in Hindi.The Prime Minister also shared a Sanskrit shlok highlighting the importance of cultivating relationships with virtuous people and promoting dialogue and goodwill.“A person should always live among the virtuous and cultivate their company. A person should engage in discussion and foster friendly relations with the virtuous, because mutual goodwill, dialogue and friendly relations strengthen peace and cooperation,” the verse said in a loose translation.As Brics chair in 2026, India will host the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of Brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.During the summit, leaders are expected to discuss ways to strengthen intra-Brics cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.Earlier on Thursday night, Bharat Mandapam, the venue for the summit in New Delhi, was being readied to host the high-profile gathering, with leaders and representatives from across the world expected to arrive for the September 12-13 event.
Article Summary: Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti- West. PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"

Article Title: "Legacy of our ancestors...": CM Pushkar Singh Dhami hails Rudrapur's transformative growth at Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan
Article Text:
"Legacy of our ancestors...": CM Pushkar Singh Dhami hails Rudrapur's transformative growth at Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday lauded the pioneering legacy and transformative contributions of the ancestors and various communities in turning Rudrapur into a vibrant industrial hub and the granary of the nation.Speaking at the Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan in Rudrapur, the chief minister expressed deep gratitude to the Sikh Gurus for the ancestral sacrifices that laid the groundwork for the state's progress."I bow in reverence at the feet of all our Gurus. I pray to the Guru Sahibs that the spirit of service towards our society and our state remains alive within all of us," he said.CM Dhami hailed the development done in Rudrapur, highlighting that this is the same region that once faced threats of venomous snakes and scorpions and deadly animals like crocodiles and tigers."Look at the wonderful work being done here; may we all continue to receive the strength to undertake such noble tasks. Every community is progressing. There was a time when people spoke of the dangers here: snakes, scorpions, massive crocodiles, tigers. Yet, it was settled and transformed into what it is today, a hub of industry and a land of lush green fields that serve as a granary, supplying food to the entire nation.This is the legacy of our ancestors; we must cherish and preserve it," he said.Meanwhile, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national president Nitin Nabin, who was also present at the programme as part of his two-day visit to the State, highlighted the Centre's interventions to protect persecuted minority communities from neighbouring nations, specifically referencing the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA).Nabin said, "We all know how there was a threat to the existence of the Sikh community in Afghanistan. A law that should have been made in the initial years of independence took a long time to be formed."Further, Nabin emphasised that the Modi government fulfilled a long-standing post-independence commitment by offering refuge and dignity to persecuted Sikhs and Hindus."With CAA (Citizenship Amendment Act), PM Narendra Modi fulfilled the promise that was made to people at the time of independence. Sikhs and Hindus who were facing atrocities in Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh are welcomed here not as refugees but as the children of this soil," he said.Earlier today, Nitin Nabin and Pushkar Singh Dhami paid floral tributes at the Shaheed Smarak in Haldwin honour of soldiers who laid down their lives for the nation.Nabin, along with CM Dhami, also offered prayers and performed rituals at the Mahalaxmi Temple in Haldwani earlier in the day. (ANI)
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday lauded the pioneering legacy and transformative contributions of the ancestors and various communities. He expressed deep gratitude to the Sikh Gurus for the ancestral sacrifices that laid the groundwork for the state's progress. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national president Nitin Nabin highlighted the Centre's interventions to protect persecuted minority communities.

The 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit is scheduled to be held in New Delhi on September 12 and 13, with leaders of the expanded grouping set to discuss global governance, multilateralism, trade, investment, technology, food and energy security, health, disaster resilience and critical supply chains. The summit will also take up major global and regional developments, including geopolitical conflicts and disruptions to global trade and energy routes.The summit is set to begin on Saturday, September 12, with a closed-door meeting of BRICS member countries at 2.35 pm on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism”. Leaders will then visit the Bharat Innovates Exhibition at 4.25 pm, followed by the official family photograph and a joint tree-planting ceremony at 5.05 pm. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for the participating leaders at 7.30 pm.On Sunday, September 13, leaders of BRICS member countries, partner countries and outreach invitees will begin arriving at 9.55 am. The official group photograph is scheduled for 10.35 am, followed by the main open session at 10.50 am, titled “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth”.The summit will conclude with the New Delhi Declaration.With a large number of foreign leaders and senior dignitaries converging on the capital, Delhi has been placed under a multilayered security grid for the summit.Around 15,000 Delhi Police personnel and 200 companies of paramilitary forces have been deployed, while 500 CCTV cameras have been installed across key locations for round-the-clock surveillance.Security arrangements are particularly tight around the diplomatic enclave and the hotels where visiting leaders will stay. China, Russia and Iran have been allotted separate hotels, with security teams from the respective countries also reaching Delhi ahead of their presidents.The heightened security measures extend beyond the summit venue. The DGCA has restricted certain flying activities across seven northern states, while the use of light and micro-light aircraft, UAVs and similar aerial vehicles has been prohibited within a 300-km radius of Delhi for 52 hours from Friday.Traffic and public movement are also expected to be regulated around key routes and venues during the summit. The New Delhi railway station will see changes to train operations over the summit period, including cancellations, diversions, rescheduling and regulation of services.The summit is expected to draw a sizable international media contingent, with around 1,200-1,300 journalists expected to cover the event. Delhi has also been decked up for the summit, with Bharat Mandapam at the centre of the two-day diplomatic gathering.The following is the arrival schedule provided for media coordination, with ETAs and designated airports:Putin was the first major head of state to arrive, landing at AFS Palam early morning on September 11. PM Modi is also scheduled to meet the Russian president today. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is arriving at Palam at 2 pm, is scheduled to meet PM Modi in the evening.Xi Jinping arrives at 12.25 pm on September 12, with the Chinese president's visit marking his first trip to India in seven years. PM Modi and Xi are scheduled to hold bilateral talks at 6 pm on Saturday.South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres are among the other prominent arrivals listed in the schedule.
Article Summary: The 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit is scheduled to be held in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. Leaders of the expanded grouping set to discuss global governance, multilateralism, trade, investment, technology and food and energy security. The summit will also take up major global and regional developments, including geopolitical conflicts and disruptions to global trade and routes.

Article Title: UP in SC: Magistrate who sent notice to student suspended
Article Text: NEW DELHI: UP govt informed Supreme Court Thursday that it has suspended the executive magistrate who issued a peace bond notice to a second-year law student in Noida for participating in the NEET-UG paper leak student protest and clarified that the district magistrate had no role in the offending action.This information was given by solicitor general Tushar Mehta when a counsel mentioned that the law student has filed a petition challenging the action of the executive magistrate despite clear orders from SC on Sept 1 quashing all FIRs, banning fresh FIRs and taking any coercive step against students.The counsel said that a message must go to IAS and IPS officers on how to comply with SC orders. When the counsel repeatedly referred to the district magistrate, Mehta said: "It was some other officer, who has been suspended by govt. Let us not sensationalise the incident."
Article Summary: UP govt informed Supreme Court Thursday that it has suspended the executive magistrate who issued a peace bond notice to a second-year law student in Noida. This information was given by solicitor general Tushar Mehta when a counsel mentioned that the law student has filed a petition challenging the action.

Article Title: Congress-NC rift over Vande Mataram: The ghost of 1987 and ‘big brother’ complex
Article Text:
The 1987 ghost: Vande Mataram row and why Omar Abdullah won't let Congress call the shots in J&K.

Venugopal called on allies to honour the wisdom of the freedom fighters

One alliance, two political vocabularies

Congress and the National Conference have had a stop-start relationship since 1965

The alliance and an unequal power equation

What Omar Abdullah had said in 2024

The Rajya Sabha dispute

The ghost of 1987

1987: The alliance that became a warning

2009-14: History managed, but not erased

The 1987 ghost & real test of alliance

The latest Congress-National Conference (NC) clash may have begun with a song, but it is really about something much older: who gets to set the political terms of the alliance in Jammu and Kashmir?CM Omar Abdullah and NC president Farooq Abdullah stood through the full rendition of Vande Mataram on Wednesday at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar. The song was played in its complete six-stanza version, lasting about three minutes and 10 seconds, in line with the Centre's new protocol.This was in sharp contrast with the Congress's stand. Its grand-old party has reaffirmed its 1937 decision to restrict public rendition at party events to the first two stanzas, arguing that the later verses sit uneasily with the pluralist ethos of the freedom movement.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal subsequently said the full version "sits uneasily" with the syncretic and pluralist ethos envisioned by India's freedom fighters and urged allies to stand by the Congress position.The NC was quick to respond, saying the J&K government was only fulfilling its official duty. "After legislative enactment by Parliament, singing Vande Mataram and standing for the song has become a statutory obligation (mandatory legal duty) regardless of the ideological position of any party, group or alliance," said National Conference spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq.A day later, CM Omar Abdullah also defended the move and said the issue had been needlessly politicised."This is not just for Jammu and Kashmir; it applies to the entire country. In states governed by the Congress, the same will happen at government functions," he said."This is now a statutory obligation. Even today, at the closing ceremony, a Union minister will be present. The national anthem will be played there, and the national song will be played too," he added.The Vande Mataram row is the latest in the list of NC-Congress differences that have surfaced post-election. However, in J&K, the dispute carries an additional historical charge.The NC has spent decades constructing its political identity around a particular proposition: New Delhi can be a partner, but it cannot be the political proprietor of Kashmir's choices.That is where the ghost of 1987 enters.The Vande Mataram dispute has once again exposed an asymmetry that has repeatedly surfaced between the two parties.Congress has to balance its position across India. For Abdullahs' NC, the principal political constituency remains rooted in J&K, where questions of identity, autonomy, federalism and the relationship with New Delhi carry a much more immediate electoral meaning.It is also why the latest row is not an isolated irritant in the alliance.In December 2025, for instance, Omar Abdullah explicitly distanced the NC from Congress's "vote chori" campaign, saying Congress was free to choose its own agenda but that it was not automatically the agenda of the INDIA bloc. With this, Omar tried to assert his party's political autonomy within the alliance.And that has been the recurring pattern.The 2024 assembly election gave the NC-Congress relationship a new lease of life, but it also made the asymmetry between the two parties stark.The alliance crossed the majority mark with 49 seats, with the NC winning 42, Congress six and CPM one. The BJP emerged with 29, PDP three and independents seven.The pre-poll negotiations themselves had not been effortless: the parties agreed that NC would contest 51 seats and Congress 32, while several constituencies remained "friendly contests".The campaign also revealed the limits of joint ownership. Congress and NC leaders did not always campaign together. In Sopore, where the two allies were in a friendly contest, Rahul Gandhi and Omar Abdullah campaigned for their respective candidates separately.During the campaign, Omar Abdullah had publicly noted that Rahul Gandhi should dedicate more campaign time and effort to the Jammu region in addition to Kashmir to maximise electoral impact.Omar himself gave the practical reason for the alliance during the campaign: it was intended to prevent a hung assembly and give voters an alternative.The alliance won the election, and the next question was: what does each side get to claim as its own?The first major post-election rupture came even before the new government had settled in.Omar Abdullah became CM in October 2024, but Congress chose to stay out of his ministry, citing restoration of statehood as its priority. While Congress backed the NC government from outside, its absence highlighted a strategic divide within the alliance. Omar had to engage with Delhi to govern the Union Territory, while Congress sought to pressure the Centre from outside. That difference in approach has repeatedly resurfaced.In July 2025, Congress announced protests in Jammu, Srinagar and Delhi and Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to PM Narendra Modi seeking legislation to restore J&K's statehood. The NC leadership was irritated because the announcement had not been coordinated with the ruling party. Some NC leaders described Congress's campaign as counterproductive and even as "sabotage" of the government's own efforts.Omar's objection was that Congress had launched the campaign without informing or consulting the NC, leaving its alliance partner caught off guard.The difference is clearer on Article 370 . The NC's 2024 manifesto explicitly called for the restoration of Articles 370 and 35A and reversal of the changes made after August 2019. Congress has similarly opposed the 2019 constitutional changes, but in its recent campaigns placed greater emphasis on the restoration of statehood.Omar reiterated in the J&K assembly in February that his government remained committed to restoring special status, even as statehood remained an immediate demand. By July 2026, he was also linking the restoration of statehood to any future discussion on J&K's earlier constitutional position.This has given the two parties different political priorities.In October 2025, the disagreement moved from ideology to seats. J&K was electing four Rajya Sabha members. The NC, which had emerged as the dominant party in the assembly, initially discussed leaving one seat for Congress.Talks failed.The NC eventually fielded candidates for all four seats after Congress decided not to contest the fourth seat it had been offered, arguing that it was not among the "safe seats" it had sought.Omar's response was strikingly matter-of-fact: "So be it."The NC-Congress disagreement ultimately cost the alliance a clean sweep, with the BJP winning the fourth seat Congress had declined to contest.To understand why the NC may be particularly sensitive to questions of control, one has to go back not merely to 1987 but to 1984.Farooq Abdullah's government was dismissed on July 2, 1984, after 12 NC legislators defected. Ghulam Mohammad Shah, Farooq's brother-in-law and leader of the defecting group, formed the government with Congress support. Contemporary accounts described the episode as a central-government intervention in Kashmir politics; Farooq called the dismissal unconstitutional.For the NC, this was not an abstract constitutional episode. It was a direct lesson in the vulnerability of a regional government to New Delhi's political machinery.Then came 1986.Rajiv Gandhi and Farooq Abdullah reached an agreement that brought the two parties together electorally. A Human Rights Watch report noted that the accord deepened a sense of betrayal among many Kashmiris, who saw Farooq Abdullah compromising with the same Congress party that had pushed him out of office two years earlier.The NC-Congress alliance won 66 of J&K's 76 assembly seats in 1987. But the result was overshadowed by the emergence of the Muslim United Front as an opposition platform, arrests of its candidates and workers, and widespread allegations of electoral rigging. Human Rights Watch later described the election as a turning point that contributed to widespread disillusionment with electoral politics.The significance of 1987 for the NC, therefore, is about the political memory it created. A generation of Kashmiri activists came to believe that the democratic route had been closed to them, a perception that became part of the backdrop to the insurgency that followed.The episode also left an enduring paradox. Congress was simultaneously the NC's electoral partner and a major force at the Centre. That history helps explain the NC's instinct to work with Congress while resisting any perception that Delhi is dictating its regional agenda.That distrust predates the 1980s. In 1953, Sheikh Abdullah was dismissed and arrested after his relationship with the Union government deteriorated. The circumstances were very different, but the political memory was similar: central intervention could reshape J&K's politics. For the NC, unlike many other regional parties, Congress's centralising past is therefore not distant history but part of its own political inheritance.The two parties showed they could overcome that history after the 2008 assembly election. The NC won 28 seats and Congress 17, and the parties formed a coalition government with Omar Abdullah as CM in 2009.But the partnership remained contested. Differences over AFSPA, administrative issues and governance repeatedly surfaced. In 2011, Congress called for consensus on AFSPA while Omar maintained that the state government was an important stakeholder.By 2014, the alliance had run its course and Congress chose to contest the assembly election separately. NC leaders argued that the association with a centrist national party had diluted the party's pro-Valley credentials, with one senior NC leader calling Congress a "very bad alliance partner".While 1987 may still shape the NC's political instincts, it would be too simplistic to link every present-day disagreement to that history. The political and constitutional context has changed; however, the experience remains part of the backdrop to the relationship.The lesson for the NC, as we saw in the last election, has not been to avoid Congress, but to work with it where interests converge while retaining its own political space.The Vande Mataram dispute, therefore, is less significant in itself than what it reveals about continuing differences over statehood, Article 370, seat-sharing and the balance between Congress's national strategy and the NC's regional politics.The alliance can survive such differences, but the interesting question now is how durable it will be, which willdepend on how well the two parties manage their competing political priorities.
Article Summary: Congress and the National Conference have had a stop-start relationship since 1965. Omar Abdullah and Farooq Abdullah stood through the full rendition of Vande Mataram at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar. The song was played in its complete six-stanza version, lasting about three minutes and 10 seconds, in line with the Centre's new protocol. This was in sharp contrast with the Congress's stand.

Article Title: Two taxi drivers held for schoolgirl's abduction-rape in Poonch
Article Text:
Representative image

JAMMU: J&K Police arrested two taxi drivers for allegedly abducting a Class VII student in Poonch’s Mendhar last week and gang-raping her in captivity for three days.Police said the survivor, aged around 13-14 years, is a resident of Mendhar’s Gursai and studies at a govt school in Surankote.The two accused are friends and drive pooled cabs. Both are in their late 20s and from Gursai, police said.According to the police complaint filed by the minor’s father at Gursai PS on Wednesday, his daughter was returning from school on Sept 6 when she boarded the pooled cab driven by one of the accused. Instead of stopping at the designated destination, the driver took her to his residence, where he and his friend allegedly confined and raped her repeatedly for three days.“An FIR was registered against the accused duo under the Pocso Act and BNS provisions for gang-rape, kidnapping and wrongful confinement,” an official said. Police said further investigation was under way.
Article Summary: Police said the survivor, aged around 13-14 years, is a resident of Mendhar’s Gursai. She studies at a govt school in Surankote. The two accused are friends and drive pooled cabs. Both are in their late 20s and from Mendhar, police said.

Article Title: Omar Abdullah defends NC MLA in pyjama row, BJP alleges bid to propagate myths
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah slipped into the pyjama row stoked by NC legislator Tanvir Sadiq this week, declaring Thursday that various historical accounts validate his claim about Dogra-governed Kashmir being so poor that an entire rural mohalla would own a single pair of pyjamas for residents to share when they needed to travel.“Even Sir Walter Lawrence (British civil servant and author) has talked about it. Kashmiris were suppressed deeply by landlords. Tanvir is not the first to say it. There was indeed a time when Kashmiris had to collect a pyjama from the local mosque to visit the city,” Omar said. “We have now come out of such poverty. We educate our children now.”The CM’s defence of his colleague and party spokesperson came a day after BJP workers burnt effigies of the latter over his Sept 8 remark, coinciding with the death anniversary of NC founder Sheikh Abdullah.“Our elders say Kashmiris didn’t have pyjamas to wear and one pyjama was shared by an entire mohalla during Dogra rule,” Sadiq had said, crediting Sheikh Abdullah’s land reforms in the 1950s with transforming the lives of Kashmiris.BJP accused Sadiq of insulting Kashmiri women, terming the remark an attempt to “glorify Abdullah through NC propaganda at the cost of Kashmir’s dignity”.PDP also demanded an apology, with senior party functionary Naeem Akhtar saying NC’s stand betrayed its allegedly feudal views.“They convey that progress was possible because of one party and one man, irrespective of the fact that similar reforms took place in other parts of the world at the time,” he said.Sadiq refused to apologise, citing references in Lawrence’s book The Valley of Kashmir. Lawrence, who arrived in J&K in 1889, wrote that he found the people “sullen, desperate and suspicious”.“They had been taught for years that they were serfs without rights…Pages might be written by me on facts which have come under my personal observation, but it will suffice to say that the system of administration has degraded the people and taken all heart out of them,” the NC legislator quoted from the book.Gul Wani, former head of the political science department at University of Kashmir, said the references should be read “as a metaphor for conditions in an agrarian society crushed by extreme poverty and excessive landlordism”.
Article Summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah says historical accounts validate his claim about Dogra- governed Kashmir being so poor that an entire rural mohalla would own a single pair of pyjamas for residents to share. “Even Sir Walter Lawrence (British civil servant and author) has talked about it. Kashmiris were suppressed deeply by landlords,” Omar said.

NEW DELHI: Ladakh groups have expressed disappointment after a meeting with the ministry of home affairs sub-committee, saying the Centre failed to present the much-awaited draft for a proposed elected body for the Union Territory.Climate activist and Leh Apex Body (LAB) member Sonam Wangchuk said there had been “no special progress” since the May 22 meeting, while Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) representative Sajjad Kargili said the delegation had come to Delhi expecting a draft detailing the structure and powers of the proposed body.The LAB and KDA have been seeking an elected legislative body at the UT level and safeguards for land, jobs, culture and identity since talks with the Centre began in 2021, news agency PTI reported.Kargili said the meeting reiterated that the proposed body would be elected, with separate delimitation and constituencies. Article Title: 'Can't browbeat child': SC on CJP protester's intimidation complaint against 'influencer'
Article Text:
SC directs protection for minor CJP protester, warns against ‘browbeating’ victim

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday took serious note of allegations that a 14-year-old girl associated with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests was harassed and that her residence was subjected to stone pelting, directing authorities to act on her FIR and provide protection to her and her family.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to ensure action on the girl's FIR and sought status reports from the Delhi and Uttar Pradesh governments on the allegations, security arrangements and action taken against those allegedly involved.The court stressed that nobody could be allowed to intimidate a victim or her family to prevent them from pursuing criminal proceedings."Such matters cannot be taken lightly. Nobody should be protected if violence against a child is involved... if persons accused of such acts were roaming free and attempting to browbeat the child or her family so that they do not pursue criminal proceedings, it would be a serious matter."There cannot be any second opinion about it. Such matters cannot be taken lightly. Nobody should be protected. If violence against a child is involved and persons are roaming free and trying to browbeat the child or the family so that they do not pursue the criminal proceedings, that may be a serious matter," the bench observed.The counsel appearing for the minor told the court that she had been harassed and her house vandalised after she registered an FIR against a person who allegedly claimed in a video that he had attacked her father during the CJP's protest.The lawyer alleged that instead of prosecuting people who accompanied the accused and were allegedly captured on camera, an FIR had been registered against the child. The counsel also submitted that this was contrary to an earlier Supreme Court order and that video evidence showing stone pelting at the girl's residence could be placed before the court."The high-powered committee will take time, but if something happens to the child in the meantime, that cannot subsequently be reversed or repaired through the committee," the counsel submitted.Responding to the submission, CJI Surya Kant said, "If there are anti-social elements who indulged in violence against child, and they are roaming free, and are trying to browbeat the child, that may be a serious thing."The Chief Justice further told the Solicitor General, "Child is a child. Some measures to protect the child can be taken. This incident can be taken as a standalone [case] by local police."Justice Joymalya Bagchi also directed that immediate action be taken on the FIR and that the minor and her family be provided police protection."We would like immediate action on that FIR and police protection to victim and family by UP police. Investigation be conducted by Parliament Street PS".The counsel also alleged that videos showed four policemen accompanying the persons who attacked the protesters and claimed that no action had been taken against them.Delhi Police action against accusedThe Supreme Court proceedings came days after Delhi Police on September 5 added provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and criminal intimidation to an FIR against Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj over the alleged assault on the minor activist's father during the CJP-led protests.Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr after the CJP staged a protest outside Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest over the alleged assault.The police action followed an interview in which Bhardwaj allegedly claimed that he had "cracked the skull" of the minor activist's father during the July 20 protest and escaped arrest because of his political connections.During Thursday's hearing, Senior Advocate PV Dinesh also mentioned a plea filed by second-year law student Akshat Tripathi challenging a notice issued to him by the Executive Magistrate, Greater Noida. The notice was subsequently withdrawn.Dinesh urged the court to hear the plea, arguing that a strong message needed to be sent to IAS officers.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court took serious note of allegations that a 14-year-old girl associated with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests was harassed. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to ensure action on the girl's FIR. The court stressed that nobody could be allowed to intimidate a victim or her family to prevent them from pursuing criminal proceedings.

Article Title: No 'Nitishpur'? JD(U) sidesteps NDA partner's proposal to rename Nitish Kumar's birthplace

NEW DELHI: JD(U) on Thursday appeared to distance itself from an alliance partner’s proposal to rename Bakhtiyarpur, the birthplace of former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar , as “Nitishpur”.JD(U) working president Sanjay Kumar Jha, when asked about the proposal by Hindustani Awam Morcha (HAM) president Santosh Kumar Suman, said Kumar had never favoured renaming places.“My party and I thank him (Suman) for expressing such a sentiment. But Nitish Kumar has always let his work speak on his behalf. He has never believed in renaming places,” news agency PTI quoted JD(U) working president as saying.Jha, who is also a Rajya Sabha MP, said changing the town’s name would not alter its history. “Let us bear in mind that merely changing the name of the place will not erase from history the fact that Bakhtiyar Khilji had invaded the land and set Nalanda, the ancient seat of learning, on fire”.“We, however, take pride in the fact that it was our leader’s efforts that resulted in a modern, international university being set up in Nalanda. I recall late CPI(M) stalwart Sitaram Yechury having pointed out the glorious coincidence in Parliament that a son of Bakhtiyarpur was reviving the glory of Nalanda, eight centuries after it was ravaged by Bakhtiyar Khilji,” he added.Suman, a minister and HAM president, had proposed the renaming in a post on X on Wednesday, saying Kumar’s “life journey, struggles, and countless memories” were linked to Bakhtiyarpur.“Honouring the birthplace of such a mass leader—who paved a new path for Bihar in development, good governance, and social transformation—with his name will not just be a change of a place's name; it will be an act of respect to the pride of that soil, its history, and the public sentiments connected to it," he said.The proposal drew a sharp reaction from the RJD, with MLA Bhai Virendra mocking the suggestion. “It is preposterous to suggest that Bakhtiyarpur should be named after Nitish Kumar. It appears that the next suggestion from BJP allies would be to name the country after Narendra Modi,” he said.Nitish Kumar, 75, is the JD(U)’s national president and Bihar’s longest-serving chief minister. He stepped down as chief minister in April before being elected to the Rajya Sabha.
Article Summary: JD(U) says Nitish Kumar has never believed in renaming places after ‘Nitishpur’ proposal. Hindustani Awam Morcha president Santosh Kumar Suman had proposed the renaming in a post on X on Wednesday.

Article Title: 'You are correct, my jaw did break': Stalin breaks silence on Vijay's assembly gesture

NEW DELHI: DMK president M K Stalin on Thursday broke his silence over Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s MISA jibe and the “jaw gesture” in the Assembly, recalling the alleged abuse and severe assaults he faced during his detention under the Emergency.Stalin released a nearly 10-minute video message detailing his experience in prison, criticising the TVK government’s welfare delivery and calling for greater decorum in the House.Stalin hit out at Vijay for reviving decades-old corruption allegations based on the Sarkaria Commission report, dismissing them as "politically motivated lies" propagated by those who had long-standing grievances against former chief minister M Karunanidhi.Addressing the controversy over his detention under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) during the Emergency, Stalin acknowledged in the video posted on "X" that Vijay was correct about the history of MISA. He recalled the repression during the Emergency and his own arrest on January 31, 1976, after Karunanidhi protested against the law.Stalin recounted the harsh conditions he faced in prison, including physical abuse that he said led to the death of his colleague Chitti Babu and left him injured."I realise that some controversies that occurred in the recently concluded Legislative Assembly session have caused anger and dissatisfaction among the Tamil people and our brethren. Since my prison history is a key part of this controversy, I wish to clarify it. Brother Vijay, what you said is true; it is not a lie. During the Emergency, our leader Kalaignar (Karunanidhi) held a massive meeting at Marina Beach to oppose it and harshly criticised the MISA," Stalin said in the video.He said the then Union government dismissed the DMK government on January 31, 1976, following which police arrived at his Gopalapuram residence to arrest him under MISA.In the video message released amid the political row, Stalin described his broken jaw as an unalterable "brave scar" of history."I faced many atrocities in prison. They locked us up in a place where leprosy patients were kept. They stuffed 10 people into a small room. In that same room, we all had to relieve ourselves in a single pot. The place was very foul-smelling; that is where we had to sleep. We were not allowed to sleep at night; the police would beat us with batons and trample us with boots," Stalin said.He further alleged that life-convict inmates were made to brutally beat him and other DMK members."My dear brother and Member of Parliament Chitti Babu died in prison because of their beatings. My jawbone broke from their hits. You (Vijay) even placed your hand on your jaw to show it, and that is correct. Even today, I have the scars from those beatings. I am not saying I didn't experience it," Stalin said, adding that "fictional accounts cannot erase history."The ruling TVK hit back, demanding proof of Stalin’s detention.Rebutting the DMK president, the TVK IT Wing described his video message as an "engineered attempt" to divert attention from core governance issues. It said Stalin had failed to furnish any official evidence to substantiate his account of his detention under MISA and demanded proof of his imprisonment, accusing him of using the address to protect a "declining political image".The controversy stems from a heated exchange in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, where Vijay made a hand-to-jaw gesture during his September 7 speech while referring to MISA, drawing sharp criticism from both allies and political rivals.The opposition DMK immediately protested, triggering chaos in the House. On September 8, Vijay clarified that the gesture was unintentional.
Article Summary: DMK president M K Stalin broke his silence over Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s MISA jibe and the “jaw gesture’ in the Assembly. He recalled the alleged abuse and severe assaults he faced during his detention under the Emergency. Stalin hit out at Vijay for reviving decades-old corruption allegations based on the Sarkaria Commission report.

NEW DELHI: The Karnataka government on Thursday directed that the national song ‘ Vande Mataram ’ be played or sung at all state government programmes and official ceremonies.According to a government order dated September 8, 2026, the decision was taken in accordance with guidelines issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.The order states that, except at programmes attended by the President, Vice President, Prime Minister or Governor, only the first two stanzas of ‘Vande Mataram’ shall be sung at all state government programmes. The order was issued in the name of the governor of Karnataka.The development comes amid a political row over the rendition of ‘Vande Mataram’, after Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said the full version of the song “sits uneasily” with the syncretic and pluralist ethos envisioned by India’s freedom fighters.Venugopal urged Congress allies to respect the version of the national song adopted by the party in 1937, saying the decision to use only the first two stanzas at official party programmes was aimed at preventing the song from being “communalised”.His remarks came after Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah and National Conference president Farooq Abdullah stood through the full rendition of ‘Vande Mataram’ at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar.The issue has also drawn criticism from the BJP, with Union home minister Amit Shah earlier targeting the Congress over its adherence to the 1937 position and accusing the party of pursuing appeasement politics.

Article Title: DMK MLAs bundled out as row over Vijay’s remarks rocks Tamil Nadu assembly
Article Text:
Speaker JCD Prabhakar refused to accept DMK's demand to expunge CM Vijay's remark from assembly records

CHENNAI: DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday after a stormy confrontation over chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks on late chief minister M Karunanidhi, former Union minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission and ED dossiers relating to cases pending before courts.The dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks, prompting DMK members to raise slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats despite repeated appeals, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.The confrontation began during Zero Hour when DMK whip E V Velu raised objections to Vijay’s remarks made during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department on Monday. Velu accused the CM of making baseless allegations and referring to pending cases, saying this went against the traditions of the House.Referring to the Sarkaria Commission, Velu said late chief minister M G Ramachandran was the principal complainant but later told the commission that he had “no idea whatsoever” about the complaint and that it had been drafted by a party functionary, Kannan from Salem. “At the conclusion, Sarkaria made it clear that there was no prima facie case in all the 28 allegations.Therefore, there was no provision for filing any case,” Velu said.He referred to DK leader K Veeramani and Left leaders being booked under MISA, like DMK leader M K Stalin, and said Vijay’s remarks had demeaned their democratic struggle.Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and R Nirmalkumar defended the CM, saying Vijay had referred to the Sarkaria Commission report and other publicly available documents as part of his fight against corruption. They accused the DMK of being the “root of corruption.”Former minister Govi Chezhiaan then posed three questions to the treasury benches: whether the CM could cite ED dossiers as evidence when the cases were pending before courts? whether the Sarkaria Commission could be selectively used for political gains when it had not found anyone guilty of corruption? and why Vijay had chosen to refer to late leaders such as Murasoli Maran?With no response forthcoming from either the treasury benches or the speaker, DMK intensified its protest.The situation turned chaotic after speaker Prabhakar ruled that there was “no need to expunge the CM’s remarks”. He said Vijay had merely referred to the Sarkaria Commission, whose findings had been discussed in the House earlier, and that the CM’s speech was within the rules of the assembly.The ruling triggered a fresh round of protests, with DMK MLAs raising slogans and sitting in the well, keeping the moments tense for nearly 45 minutes, starting from 9.31am and ending at about 10.11am. In between, the speaker also cautioned minister Aadhav Arjuna for his remarks that they would also match the opposition.The speaker repeatedly asked the members to return to their seats and offered to allow Velu and deputy leader of the opposition K N Nehru to speak on the issue. But the DMK members refused to relent.“I will not reverse my ruling,” Prabhakar asserted before directing marshals to remove the protesting MLAs. He cautioned Kallakurichi MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan against approaching the Chair.Marshals entered the House at about 10.08am and physically removed several MLAs who refused to leave the well, including Kutty alias A Sudhakar of Valparai, Durai Chandrasekaran of Thiruvaiyaru and Vasantham Karthikeyan of Rishivandiyam.Later in the day, Chezhiaan moved a privilege motion against Vijay, accusing the CM of making “baseless allegations” and citing reports connected to cases pending before courts during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department.
Article Summary: Dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks. DMK members raised slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.
