NEW DELHI: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae on Wednesday filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan and requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities across Delhi.Senior advocate Ajit Kumar Sinha, in his report, said that the Satya Niketan incident assumes significance as the locality had witnessed another building collapse in April 2022, in which two people were killed and four injured.“The present incident is also required to be viewed in the context of an earlier building collapse in Satya Niketan in April 2022, in which two persons lost their lives, and four others were injured. The recurrence of such an incident in the same locality raises serious concerns regarding the effectiveness of the existing mechanism for inspection, identification of dangerous structures, and enforcement of building bye-laws”, the amicus report said.He also noted that construction-related work was being undertaken in or around the basement and that there were reports of waterlogging in the basement immediately before the latest collapse.The amicus has sought a time-bound inspection and safety audit of PGs, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments around colleges and universities across Delhi, including checks on sanctioned building plans, actual construction and number of floors, basement construction and alterations, land use, structural and fire safety, ingress and egress, and dangerous or ruinous conditions.This comes after seven people were killed when a building collapsed in Satya Niketan on Sunday.Meanwhile, Municipal Corporation of Delhi also directed its executive engineers (building) across all zones to inspect structures under their jurisdiction and submit comprehensive reports by September 10, following the deadly building collapse in south Delhi's Satya Niketan, which killed seven people, officials said.Officials said the information collected during the inspections would be incorporated into an affidavit to be filed before the Delhi High Court within 10 days.The inspections and submission of reports will be personally monitored and supervised by the additional commissioners concerned in each zone, according to the order, they added.
Article Summary: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan. He requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities.

Article Title: Mohali court acquits 2 BSF personnel in alleged dacoity conspiracy case
Article Text:
Two BSF personnel were acquitted of conspiracy charges due to insufficient evidence (AI-generated image used for representational purposes)

Two co-accused remain fugitives





MOHALI: A court of additional district and sessions judge TPS Randhawa has acquitted two BSF personnel, Prem Singh resident of Naushera Dhalla Tarantaran and Anil Kumar resident of Tungwala in Amritsar, of charges related to an alleged conspiracy to commit dacoity holding that the prosecution failed to establish any concrete link between them and the alleged conspiracy.The court of Additional Sessions Judge acquitted the two accused of charges under Sections 399, 402 and 473 of the Indian Penal Code, observing that there was no recovery of weapons or other incriminating material from their possession.The prosecution also failed to produce any call detail record (CDR) showing their contact with the other accused.The case dates back to September 1, 2015, when the police claimed to have received information that a group of persons was planning a robbery in Mohali.However, no accused was arrested at the spot.The prosecution later alleged that the accused were also involved in smuggling weapons and drugs from across the border.The court noted that, apart from disclosure statements of co-accused, there was no independent or substantive evidence connecting Prem Singh and Anil Kumar with the alleged conspiracy or cross-border arms smuggling.Jindi gets one-year sentence in arms recovery caseThe court, however, convicted Jatinder Singh alias Jindi under Section 25 of the Arms Act and sentenced him to one year in prison and a fine of Rs 3,000.According to the prosecution, Jindi was arrested in the Jalandhar Cantt area on December 31, 2015.A .30-bore pistol, 28 live cartridges and a holster were allegedly recovered from him.The court held that the recovery stood proved on the basis of the testimony of police officials and identification of the weapon and cartridges during the trial.The defence had questioned the failure to promptly send the recovered weapon for forensic examination, its production in a plastic jar and the nearly 10-year delay in obtaining sanction under Section 39 of the Arms Act.The court rejected the objections, observing that delay in obtaining sanction did not by itself invalidate the recovery and that no material prejudice had been caused to the accused.Jindi had already undergone one year, eight months and 17 days in custody during the investigation and trial.The court took the period into account while sentencing him.As he had already undergone more than the one-year sentence imposed, he had effectively served the sentence. He also deposited the Rs 3,000 fine.Gurjant Singh alias Bholu and Sandeep Singh were also arrested in December 2015 in connection with the case.The police had alleged that weapons were recovered from them and that they fired at the police party during their arrest.Both were subsequently declared proclaimed offenders during the trial. Bholu was declared a proclaimed offender on April 24, 2025.The court ordered that proceedings against them would be reopened if they were arrested or appeared before the court.
Article Summary: Two BSF personnel were acquitted of conspiracy charges due to insufficient evidence. Two co-accused remain fugitives. Jatinder Singh alias Jindi was convicted and sentenced to one year in prison and a fine of Rs 3,000.

Article Title: Mother, newborn die after delivery at UP hospital 'sealed' a year ago, run via backdoor
Article Text:
(AI Image) A woman and her newborn died after receiving treatment at a private hospital





MAU: A woman and her newborn died after she allegedly received treatment at a private hospital in Mau that had been sealed by the administration and health department last year, officials said.The hospital, Indrajeet Hospital in Ratanpura, was allegedly operating through an alternate entrance despite the main entrance being locked. The health department has now sealed the facility again after the matter came to light.Ajit Rajbhar, a resident of Targouli village in Ballia district, lodged a complaint with the chief medical officer alleging that his pregnant wife, Sarita, was admitted to the hospital on September 8 after an ASHA worker advised the family to take her there.According to the complaint, doctor Himanshu Yadav told the family that Sarita's condition was serious and advised an operation. After the delivery, the newborn died and Sarita continued to bleed, the complaint alleged.Rajbhar alleged that hospital staff refused to continue treating his wife, following which he took her to another private hospital in Mau. She was subsequently referred to Varanasi, where doctors at a private hospital declared her dead, according to the complaint.Chief Medical Officer Pankaj Rai said Indrajeet Hospital had been sealed in 2025 on the instructions of the district magistrate."The main lock was intact, but the hospital was being operated by opening a passage from the back," Rai said.After being informed about the incident, the health department, in coordination with the sub-divisional magistrate, sealed the hospital again, he said.A complaint has also been lodged against the hospital operator and steps are being taken to register an FIR, Rai said.The administration is investigating how treatment was allegedly being carried out at a facility that had already been sealed, officials said.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: A pregnant woman and her newborn died after she allegedly received treatment at a private hospital in Mau. The hospital, Indrajeet Hospital in Ratanpura, was allegedly operating through an alternate entrance despite the main entrance being locked. The health department has now sealed the facility again after the matter came to light.

Article Title: 'Stay loyal to him': Lucknow man lets wife go, marry lover
Article Text:
A PRD jawan in Malihabad accepted his wife's decision to leave him





LUCKNOW: After hours of attempts to persuade his wife to return home, a PRD personnel in Malihabad finally chose to let her go — and even helped her marry the man she wanted to be with.The woman, who had married the PRD jawan in May last year, had allegedly left her in-laws’ house a few days ago without informing her family. After failing to trace her, the husband approached Malihabad police and lodged a missing report.The matter took an unexpected turn on Wednesday when the woman reached Malihabad police station with her lover. Police said the two had been in a relationship before her marriage.The woman's arrival brought both her parental and marital families to the police station, where relatives spent several hours trying to convince her to return to her husband and resume their marriage. She, however, remained firm about wanting to live with her lover.When the reconciliation attempts failed, the husband accepted her decision and agreed to end their relationship by mutual consent. Before they parted, he reportedly told her to remain loyal to the man she had chosen.The woman and her lover later went to a nearby temple, where they got married and left together.Malihabad inspector Surendra Bhati said both families eventually accepted the woman's decision. “The matter was resolved through mutual consent. No complaint has been filed by either party,” he said.
Article Summary: The woman had married the PRD jawan in May last year. She had allegedly left her in-laws’ house a few days ago without informing her family. After failing to trace her, the husband approached Malihabad police. Police said the two had been in a relationship before her marriage.

Article Title: Bengaluru man accused of killing kids breaks down: 'Wife got new job, found chats with male colleague'
Article Text:
A 40-year-old man allegedly killed his two minor daughters before attempting suicide at a five-star hotel.





BENGALURU: “I killed them because I loved them and was worried about their future,” SG Imran told investigators after allegedly strangling his two young daughters at a hotel near Kempegowda International Airport last month.The 40-year-old manager at a local cab company broke down during a recent police reconstruction of the crime inside the hotel room, weeping uncontrollably and rolling on the floor for nearly 20 minutes as he lamented the deaths of Shaik Zoya, 10, and Shaik Zehara, 5.Imran, a resident of Bilalnagar, allegedly killed the girls on August 10 before attempting to take his own life by slitting his throat. He was shifted to a private hospital and recovered in about two weeks.During the reconstruction, police said Imran collapsed to the floor and continued sobbing. “We did not stop him or try to pacify him. We knew that he had to pour out his feelings. He wept, cried, and lamented for around 15–20 minutes, and we just watched him,” said a senior police officer handling the investigation.During interrogation, Imran admitted to the double murder and told investigators that he had been overcome by fears about his daughters’ upbringing following the breakdown of his marriage.According to police, Imran said his marriage began deteriorating around 15 months ago after his wife got a new job. He alleged that he discovered WhatsApp conversations between her and a male colleague, leading to frequent domestic disputes and eventually their separation two months before the killings.Under an informal arrangement, the children stayed with their mother on weekdays and visited Imran on weekends.Police also recovered a suicide note from the hotel room in which Imran allegedly wrote about his wife’s alleged infidelity, marital discord and the custody dispute.Police said Imran sometimes experiences mood swings. He is currently in judicial custody at Bengaluru Central Prison.
Article Summary: SG Imran allegedly strangled his two young daughters at a hotel near Kempegowda International Airport. The 40-year-old manager at a local cab company broke down during a recent police reconstruction of the crime. He told investigators that he had been overcome by fears about his daughters’ upbringing following the breakdown of his marriage.

Article Title: 'Killer' bahu’s deadly game: Kanpur bizman sensed danger but ended up with 26 stab wounds and a slit throat
Article Text:
An alleged murder plot to stage a heart attack was foiled when the victim returned home. Shalu and her husband (L) Vineet Minocha (M)

Killers allegedly waited inside bedroom

‘Heart attack’ plan goes awry

Shalu, husband were at lounge during murder

Police allege Shalu stayed in touch with assailants

CCTV dispute allegedly behind murder

No valuables stolen from apartment





KANPUR: A murder planned to look like a heart attack allegedly turned into a brutal stabbing after 63-year-old businessman Vineet Minocha walked into his bedroom and noticed something unusual. The assailants allegedly panicked, attacked him with knives and fled, leaving Vineet with 26 stab wounds and a slit throat.According to investigators, Minocha's daughter-in-law Shalu Minocha, who police have accused of masterminding the murder, had allegedly instructed former employee Vishal Gautam and his acquaintance Raj Kishor to suffocate Vineet with a pillow so the death would appear natural.But the plan allegedly changed after Vineet walked into the bedroom around 11pm and noticed something unusual.Police said Shalu had approached Vishal, a former employee at Vineet's pharmaceutical store, and allegedly offered him Rs 6 lakh for the killing.She allegedly handed Vishal the original key to the family's apartment so that a duplicate could be made. Vishal then allegedly involved his unemployed acquaintance Raj Kishor, 30, promising him an advance of Rs 30,000.On September 5, Shalu allegedly told the two men that she, her husband Subrat and their son would be attending a party.Using the duplicate key, Vishal and Raj allegedly entered Ratan Orbit Apartment in Kalyanpur. Police said they initially faced resistance from the security guard but told him they were delivering medicines.Vishal allegedly registered himself under the fictitious name Shivam.After entering the apartment, the two men allegedly hid inside a bedroom and waited for Vineet to return.Investigators said the original plan was to suffocate Vineet with a pillow and make the killing look like a heart attack.The plan allegedly went awry when Vineet entered the bedroom at around 11pm and noticed something unusual.Police said he was stabbed repeatedly and his throat was slit before the accused fled. The postmortem found 26 stab wounds on Vineet's body.Police said the murder took place sometime between 10.30pm on Saturday and 3am on Sunday, while Vineet was alone in the four-room apartment.While the alleged killing was taking place, Shalu and her husband were at Cosmozin Lounge in Tilak Nagar, police said.A video recorded by lounge staff showed Shalu dancing with Subrat to the Bollywood song “Tum To Dhokhebaaz Ho, Vaada Karke Bhool Jaate Ho”.Police said the footage confirmed their presence at the lounge that night.The lounge's CCTV DVR had no stored footage, but videos recorded by staff showed around 20-25 people, mostly couples, dancing to Bollywood songs. Shalu was seen wearing a dark purple gown while Subrat was dressed in a grey shirt.Police said Shalu's behaviour appeared normal and other guests at the lounge seemed unaware of what was allegedly unfolding at her home.Despite being at the party, Shalu allegedly remained in contact with the two men through WhatsApp calls, messages and voice calls and allegedly guided them during the crime, according to investigators.Police arrested Shalu on Monday after Vishal allegedly told them that he had killed Vineet on her instructions in return for money.Police said Shalu allegedly admitted her involvement in the presence of female police personnel after being confronted with Vishal.Investigators suspect the alleged murder was linked to a dispute over CCTV cameras installed by Vineet inside the apartment around 15-20 days before his death.Police said Shalu objected to the cameras, claiming they violated her privacy and caused her emotional distress.Investigators said CCTV footage showed Vishal and Raj leaving the apartment after the murder. The two were arrested following an encounter late Sunday.Police said nothing was stolen from the apartment, strengthening their suspicion that the killing was motivated by personal enmity rather than robbery.Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to criminal conspiracy, has also been added to the case.The investigation is continuing, with police examining the alleged communications between Shalu and the assailants and the circumstances surrounding Vineet's murder.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Vineet Minocha, 63, was stabbed 26 times and had his throat slit. His daughter- in-law Shalu allegedly masterminded the murder. She allegedly instructed Vishal Gautam and Raj Kishor to suffocate Vineet with a pillow so the death would appear natural.

Article Title: VVS, Mahesh Babu and Rajamouli among those issued SIR notices
Article Text:
Several prominent Hyderabad personalities have received notices regarding electoral roll revisions.





HYDERABAD: From Hyderabad's star former India batter VVS Laxman to internationally acclaimed director SS Rajamouli, several prominent personalities from the city figure in the Election Commission 's list of people who have been issued notices as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.A quick glance at the 'List of Persons to Whom Notices Have Been Issued (After Draft Roll Published on 17-08-2026)' shows several prominent personalities on the list. The exhaustive VIP list was highlighted on X platform by the handle @avinashmohan.TOI's independent check revealed that along with Laxman and Rajamouli, the list includes sportspersons Pullela Gopichand, Saina Nehwal and Mithali Raj; actors Mahesh Babu and his wife Namrata, Venkatesh Daggubati and his two daughters, Samantha Akkineni, and Vijay Deverakonda and his brother Anand, among others.Name mismatchThe reasons cited include name mismatch, 'unmapped with last SIR' and parent-name mismatch. For some, the reason for discrepancy column is blank.The list also includes entrepreneurs Murali Krishna Prasad Divi and Upasana Konidela, among others."There is an option, especially in the case of VIPs, to authorise someone to appear for the hearing if they are unavailable. There is still time, and many well-known people are yet to appear for hearings," said RV Karnan, district election officer, Hyderabad, under whose jurisdiction many of the assembly constituencies where these personalities are registered as voters fall.Officials also said it was not surprising that many well-known personalities had been issued notices, as they too, along with lakhs of voters in the state, had discrepancies in their details.Activists, meanwhile, said that if celebrities are issued notices and are at risk of losing their votes, it raises questions about what common people may be facing."What is the status of the single woman living in a small hamlet in a remote village in Telangana? Who will take responsibility if her vote gets deleted?" said Ruchith Asha Kamal, an activist who also took part in the CJP movement in Delhi.
Article Summary: Several prominent Hyderabad personalities have received notices regarding electoral roll revisions. The reasons cited include name mismatch, 'unmapped with last SIR' and parent-name mismatch. The list also includes sportspersons Pullela Gopichand, Saina Nehwal and Mithali Raj.

Article Title: Toddler in blood-stained clothes leads cops to murdered grandmom
Article Text:
(AI image) A woman was murdered and her daughter seriously injured in their Dewas home.





INDORE: A 55-year-old woman was allegedly murdered and her daughter seriously injured in their house in Satwas area of Dewas on Wednesday night, with the crime coming to light only on Thursday afternoon after the woman's three-year-old granddaughter was found wandering outside in blood-stained clothes.The toddler had apparently remained inside the house for several hours with her injured mother and dead grandmother before she was noticed by people in the neighbourhood. Police suspect the child may have been asleep for much of the time and woke up later, while her mother, though conscious, was too badly injured to get up and seek help.SP Puneet Gehlot said the deceased woman's daughter was found seriously injured inside the house. After being alerted, police reached the spot and took the injured woman to hospital, where her statement was recorded.Based on the information provided by her, police detained two persons for questioning. Both are residents of Satwas, sources said.The incident took place at the family's house in Punarwas area on Punarasa Road. The woman had come to her mother's place for Rakshabandhan and had stayed back. A police team, including senior officers, reached the spot after the toddler was found and began examining the circumstances in which the attack took place.A knife was recovered from the house, and a forensic science laboratory team was called to examine the scene. Investigators are also questioning people in the neighbourhood.Sources said a possible robbery angle is also being examined, though police have not yet established the motive or confirmed whether valuables were taken from the house.The deceased had owned the land that had been leased out and reportedly was dependent on the income from it for household expenses.Police are now trying to establish what happened between Wednesday night, when the attack is suspected to have taken place, and Thursday afternoon, when the child's presence led to the crime being discovered.
Article Summary: A 55-year-old woman was allegedly murdered and her daughter seriously injured in their house in Dewas on Wednesday night. The woman's granddaughter was found wandering outside in blood-stained clothes on Thursday afternoon. Police suspect the child may have been asleep for much of the time and woke up later, while her mother was too badly injured to get up and seek help.

Article Title: How 'white-coat terror' module unfolded: Al-Falah doctors first tested bombs inside university, then in Aravalis
Article Text:
(From Left) Ganaie poses with a weapon, Muzamil Shakeel Ganaie posing with a gun, Muzamil Shakeel Ganaie testing a weapon

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most important step to prevent such terror networks? Stronger monitoring and intelligence Strict action against those involved 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GURGAON: Test blasts on Al-Falah University campus, in open field, experiments deep inside the Aravalis, allegedly marked the progression of a “white-coat” terror module linked to three Al-Falah University doctors, according to the NIA chargesheet in the Red Fort blast case.Dr Umer Un Nabi, Dr Muzammil Shakeel Ganaie and Dr Adeel Ahmed Rather allegedly tested explosive mixtures and firearms in isolated locations around Faridabad as they moved from experimenting with fertiliser-based explosives to preparing larger quantities of IEDs. The module is accused of being behind the suicide bombing near the Red Fort on Nov 10 last year that killed 15 people and injured 29 others.The explosives trail began close to Al-Falah University. In September-October last year, Umer, Ganaie and Jasir Bilal Wani, a student accused of assisting the module, allegedly tested nitro-glycerine near a tubewell on the campus. The explosive had reportedly been prepared at Ganaie’s flat.The group then moved its experiments outside the university, carrying out test blasts in an isolated field before venturing deeper into the Faridabad Aravalis. In a forested area of Dhauj, Umer and Ganaie allegedly conducted further tests using TATP (triacetone triperoxide). NIA said remnants of a pipe-like device used in one such test were later recovered at Ganaie’s instance.The chargesheet said the module initially worked with fertiliser-based mixtures before shifting to TATP after tests demonstrated its destructive potential. The experiments eventually progressed to the preparation of larger quantities of IEDs.The weapons trail ran parallel to the explosives experiments. NIA alleged that Dr Shaheen Shahid, an associate professor in Al-Falah’s pharmacology department, provided around Rs 16 lakh to members of Ansar Ghazwat-ul-Hind (AGuH), a militant outfit founded in Kashmir in 2016 and linked to al-Qaida’s ideology. The agency alleged that the money, routed through Ganaie, was used to procure a Krinkov rifle, an AK-47 and two pistols.During Adeel’s visit to Al-Falah in October-November 2024, Ganaie, Adeel and Shaheen allegedly test-fired the Krinkov in another forested area of Dhauj. NIA further alleged that rented premises in Khori Jamalpur and Dhauj were later used to store chemicals, equipment and explosives away from public view.The procurement of material was also allegedly systematic. Umer, Ganaie, Shaheen and Wani visited markets in Gurgaon and Faridabad to buy fertilisers, chemicals, electrical equipment, trolley bags, collapsible water bags, gas stoves and other material needed for the preparations. The items were initially kept in flats on the Al-Falah campus before being shifted to rented premises near Dhauj.Wani, a Qazigund resident and political science graduate, allegedly provided technical assistance to the group. NIA said he repeatedly visited Al-Falah, helped prepare explosives and assisted in shifting raw materials to rented premises. He also allegedly prepared rocket-type IEDs while staying in Umer’s room.By early 2025, the module had allegedly fabricated several “suitcase-type IEDs” and shifted part of the stock to another rented property in Dhauj. A major cache was subsequently recovered from Fatehpur Taga, where around 2,600kg of ammonium nitrate was seized on Nov 9, a day before the Red Fort blast.Umer, identified by NIA as the suicide bomber, was killed when the i20 he was driving exploded near the crowded metro station. The blast killed 15 people and injured 29 others.The chargesheet also shed light on why Umer allegedly continued working at Al-Falah despite receiving a higher-paying job offer in Pathankot. According to NIA, the university gave him access to chemicals, fertilisers, electrical equipment, vehicles, firearms and members of AGuH.“That is because if Umer had chosen to move out of Al-Falah, his entire racket for hatching conspiracy with the co-accused and others would not have taken shape,” the chargesheet stated.
Article Summary: Dr Umer Un Nabi, Dr Muzammil Shakeel Ganaie and Dr Adeel Ahmed Rather allegedly tested explosive mixtures and firearms in isolated locations. The module is accused of being behind the suicide bombing near the Red Fort on Nov 10 last year that killed 15 people and injured 29 others.

Article Title: Secunderabad Cantonment armoury heist insider job, most weapons traced
Article Text:
Investigators have concluded the Secunderabad arms heist was an insider job. (File pic)





HYDERABAD: Eleven days after the sensational arms heist at the Madras Regiment armoury in Secunderabad Cantonment, TOI has reliably learnt that investigators have concluded it was an insider job. It is learnt that most of the weapons have been traced, according to sources.Telangana police brass refused to disclose details when contacted. One top police officer, however, said: "We got a strong lead. Give us time."From the beginning, police suspected it was an inside job. Someone part of the sentry detail was behind the heist. However, investigators were yet to ascertain details like how many of them were involved in the conspiracy and how the weapons were shifted out of the armoury.Multiple agencies, like Counter-Intelligence of Telangana, Military Intelligence, Malkajgiri police, Hyderabad Task Force, NIA, and other central agencies were involved in the investigation. On the night of Aug 30, a security breach was noticed in two separate rooms of the armoury. The accused stole four AK-203 rifles, one INSAS rifle and seven pistols. Ammunition, along with a binocular, was also stolen from other room.The unprecedented development sent shock waves through security establishments and triggered a multi-agency investigation into how such a major security breach could have occurred at a military armoury.
Article Summary: Most of the weapons have been traced, according to sources. Telangana police brass refused to disclose details when contacted. One top police officer, however, said: "We got a strong lead. Give us time" The accused stole four AK-203 rifles, one INSAS rifle and seven pistols.

Article Title: ‘Don’t break wall, building could collapse’: Plumber warned hours before Satya Niketan PG tragedy
Article Text:
A plumber warned against breaking a load-bearing wall before the Satya Niketan building collapsed.





NEW DELHI: Hours before the Satya Niketan building collapsed, a plumber working at the property had warned that breaking a load-bearing wall could bring down the structure, but the warning was allegedly ignored, police said.The warning emerged during the investigation into the collapse and is being verified by police. A police source said the plumber had cautioned the accused against breaking the wall after noticing the construction work at the property.“During the investigation, we found out that one of the plumbers had warned the accused hours before the incident not to break the wall as it could lead to a collapse. However, the warning was allegedly ignored. We are verifying the testimony and other details related to the sequence of events,” the source said.Sources said the load-bearing wall was allegedly removed during construction and may have weakened the structure, contributing to its collapse.During questioning, PG operator Sudhanshu Lovneesh, 31, allegedly told investigators that he had asked Mahesh, the building owner’s son, about the construction and why it was being carried out.Police, however, have so far found nothing to corroborate his claim.Investigators are questioning neighbours and others in the area to establish whether they had noticed the construction activity or raised concerns before the collapse. They are also reconstructing the sequence of work carried out at the property and examining the roles of those involved.A senior police officer, when asked about a purported letter sent by police to the government seeking an inspection of PGs in Satya Niketan over alleged lack of fire safety measures a few months ago, said he was not aware of the specific communication. The officer said such letters could also be part of routine correspondence between police and other departments.Police are also conducting raids to trace the associate of the PG operator.
Article Summary: A plumber working at the property had warned that breaking a load-bearing wall could bring down the structure, police said. The warning emerged during the investigation into the collapse and is being verified by police. PG operator Sudhanshu Lovneesh allegedly told investigators that he had asked Mahesh, the building owner’s son, about the construction.

Article Title: After outrage, BJP neta’s school junks food curbs during Jain fest
Article Text:
The controversy intensified on Thursday after MNS Thane district president Avinash Jadhav visited the school.





BHAYANDER: Seven Square Academy, a CBSE school run by a trust belonging to the family of BJP MLA Narendra Mehta, on Thursday withdrew a controversial circular asking students not to bring food containing onion, garlic, potato, beetroot and other such vegetables during the Jain Paryushan festival.The circular, uploaded on the school’s online portal, had triggered strong opposition from parents, political parties and social organisations. The school had also stated that these food items would not be available in its canteen during the Paryushan period.The controversy intensified on Thursday after MNS Thane district president Avinash Jadhav visited the school and warned of an agitation if the circular was not withdrawn within 24 hours. The Marathi Ekikaran Samiti also said it would initiate legal proceedings seeking cancellation of the school’s recognition.Several organisations and parents had opposed the move, questioning the decision to impose food restrictions on students during a religious festival. State transport minister Pratap Sarnaik of the Shiv Sena also criticised Mehta, calling the move hypocrisy. Sarnaik questioned whether similar restrictions were imposed at Mehta’s clubs and hotels and took a dig at the BJP over the observance of Hindu fasting days.Following the backlash, the school removed the circular from its portal late on Thursday. The MNS and Marathi Ekikaran Samiti welcomed the decision.Mehta, meanwhile, sought to clarify that the circular was only an appeal to students and was not meant to be mandatory.
Article Summary: Seven Square Academy, a CBSE school run by a trust belonging to the family of BJP MLA Narendra Mehta, on Thursday withdrew a controversial circular. circular asked students not to bring food containing onion, garlic, potato, beetroot and other such vegetables during the Jain Paryushan festival.

Article Title: ‘Suspicion cannot take place of proof’: Bombay high court frees man in physiotherapist’s 2016 rape-murder case
Article Text:
The Bombay High Court overturned a conviction and death sentence for a man.





MUMBAI: Setting aside the conviction and death sentence of a man (then 29) in the Dec 2016 rape and murder of a physiotherapist (24) in a Mumbai suburb, Bombay High Court held that the prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that he committed the offence.“The evidence led by the prosecution in support of the charge levelled against the accused, in our view, consists of weak, disconnected and/or unequivocal circumstances and in the wake of the nature of such evidence, merely based on suspicion, however strong, cannot take place of proof,” said Justices Bharati Dangre and Manjusha Deshpande in the Sept 7 verdict uploaded on Thursday. They dismissed the state’s death sentence confirmation plea and ordered Debashish Dhara “to be set at liberty. ”The victim stayed with her family in a chawl. She slept in a separate mezzanine room in front of her house. On Dec 6 around 3 am, a neighbour alerted her parents about smoke coming from her room which was bolted from outside. After dousing the fire, she was found with jeans wrapped around her neck. Dhara, employed in a nearby jewellery store, was apprehended on Jan 28, 2017, from Kolkata.On Oct 10, 2019, additional sessions judge A D Deo found Dhara guilty of several charges, including rape, murder and unnatural sexual offences.He held that the crime fell in the “rarest of rare category” for the “gruesome, ghastly or horrendous act” executed with “extreme mental perversion.”HC noted that the sessions court had held that the prosecution had established a chain of circumstances linking him to the crime. Prosecutor Tanveer Khan relied on chemical analysis/DNA report of bloodstains found on Dhara’s jeans and a comb that matched the victim’s sample and on CCTV footage. Advocate Siddharth Jagushte, for the victim’s father, said DNA profiling established Dhara was the author of the crime. Dhara’s advocate Yug Chaudhary argued that the prosecution failed to establish his guilt from evidence on record.“Right from the needle of suspicion being pointed” to Dhara, the judges found many loopholes in the prosecution’s case. As the CCTV footage did not establish in whose house Dhara was peeping and why, this cannot be an incriminating circumstance. His jeans were seized two months after the murder from the room where he lived and worked with his employer. Bloodstains were not found on the jeans but inside the right pocket, which HC found was “an innovative idea. ” While the panchnama said it was a red design on the comb’s handle, the chemical analyser said it was a bloodstain. The judges found it impossible that DNA obtained from the wet bedsheet remained intact and was compared with Dhara’s DNA. They also doubted the manner of collection and preservation of Dhara’s DNA sample.HC said the prosecution case relied on circumstances pointing to the guilt of the accused and they “are inconsistent with the reasonable hypothesis of innocence.” As a “cumulative effect,” Dhara was entitled to be set at liberty by applying the test: “In the halls of justice, the quest for truth must outshine the desire for victory.”
Article Summary: The Bombay High Court overturned a conviction and death sentence for a man. Debashish Dhara was found guilty of the rape and murder of a 24-year-old physiotherapist in a Mumbai suburb. The court held that the prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that he committed the offence.

Article Title: Several women among 9 dead after pickup van rams truck in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Nine migrant labourers died early Friday after their pickup van collided with a truck.





NAGPUR: Around nine migrant labourers, most of them women, were killed in the early hours of Friday when a pickup van rammed into a truck on the Lakhni-Pimpalgaon road in Bhandara district.Around 15 labourers were travelling in the pick-up vehicle towards Nagpur when the collision occurred. Most of them were asleep at the time, said sources.Eight of the injured were declared dead at Bhandara Government Hospital. Four others were referred to Government Medical College and Hospital in Nagpur. One of the survivors was reported to be in a critical condition.The identities of the dead and injured have not yet been established. Police and district officials said they were trying to contact family members of the labourers, who hail from Chhattisgarh.The impact was so severe that JCBs had to be used to separate the tangled vehicles."Several workers remained trapped inside and could be heard crying for help. Local villagers and police rushed to the spot and shifted the injured to government hospitals in Bhandara," said an official.IG Nagpur Range Sandeep Patil, Bhandara SP Nurul Hasan and other senior officers reached the site as rescue work continued. Bhandara district administration is providing assistance to the victims and coordinating efforts to identify them and inform their families.
Article Summary: Around 15 labourers were travelling in the pick-up vehicle towards Nagpur when the collision occurred. Most of them were asleep at the time, said sources. Eight of the injured were declared dead at Bhandara Government Hospital. One of the survivors was reported to be in a critical condition.

Article Title: 'Smashed heads with stone': Jaipur man kills wife, 3 daughters; flees after collecting milk from delivery man
Article Text:
A man allegedly killed his wife and three daughters in Jaipur's Kardhani area.





JAIPUR: A man allegedly killed his wife and three daughters by repeatedly striking them on the head with a stone at their home in Jaipur’s Kardhani area early Friday, then fled after collecting milk from a deliveryman, police said.The victims were identified as Geeta Jha and her daughters Nandini, Radhika and Gauri. Their bodies were found at thier house in Govind Vatika after police received information around 10am.Police said preliminary investigation pointed to a possible family dispute as the motive. Police and an FSL team reached the house and began examining the scene.Investigators suspect Rahul attacked the four while they were asleep, using a stone. Police said blood at the scene appeared to have been wiped with clothes after the killings.According to police, Rahul collected milk from the milkman around 7am and fled soon afterwards. His elderly father was found inside the house.Police are searching for Rahul and are examining the circumstances leading up to the killings.
Article Summary: Victims identified as Geeta Jha and her daughters Nandini, Radhika and Gauri. Their bodies were found at thier house in Govind Vatika. Police said blood at the scene appeared to have been wiped with clothes after the killings.

Article Title: Now, SIR confusion over Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar’s mom, Zerodha’s Kamaths
Article Text:
Electoral roll name mismatches are causing confusion for several prominent Bengaluru families.





BENGALURU: Instances of name mismatch in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls continue to create waves of confusion among VIP families. Days after Bharat Ratna CNR Rao and actor Shivarajkumar figured in the verification exercise, it’s the turn of the Karnataka chief minister’s mother and Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to produce documents over logical discrepancies in voter records.In none of these cases, VIPs and their family members were called to the BBMP offices.While the Nilekani family has completed verification, Zerodha’s Kamath brothers and their mother are awaiting clarity.Bengaluru South district election officers said the name of DK Shivakumar ’s mother Gowramma was flagged for mismatch in Kanakapura assembly constituency. However, she was not among those served notice. “The confusion arose from names with similar spellings. Reports on the visual media are not factually correct,” an officer said.Officials said three voters named Gowramma are listed in part no. 249 of Kanakapura constituency. The CM’s mother, Gowramma w/o Kempegowda, is listed at serial no. 1 with EPIC ZVG4032298. Notices were issued to the other two voters with the same name.In the case of the Nilekanis, SIR verification was completed Thursday. Officials said notices had been generated for Nilekani and his family under the no-mapping category.Since Nilekani falls under the VIP category, the booth-level officer visited his residence to complete verification.Nilekani’s staff sought copies of the notices before submitting documents, including details of the family’s enrolment in the 2002 rolls. The BLO later delivered the notices and returned on Thursday to collect the documents and complete the process. The Nilekanis are enrolled in Koramangala under BTM Layout assembly constituency.Ramesh KN, additional district election officer, Bengaluru South, said there was confusion over reports of notices issued to Zerodha founders Nikhil and Nithin Kamath. Officials from Bengaluru South City Corporation and urban district administration contacted their mother, Revathi Kamath, who clarified that the family had not received any notices. “We are verifying whether notices were generated in their names,” he said. Nithin, Nikhil and Revathi Kamath have been flagged over parents’ name mismatch in Bengaluru South constituency.
Article Summary: Bengaluru South district election officers said the name of DK Shivakumar ’s mother Gowramma was flagged for mismatch in Kanakapura assembly constituency. Notices were issued to the other two voters with the same name. Zerodha’s Kamath brothers and their mother are awaiting clarity.

Article Title: CM Vijay skips VIP gate at Chennai airport after advisor denied special entry for London trip
Article Text:
For his upcoming London trip, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has decided to enter through the regular passenger terminal, defying VIP access.





CHENNAI: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is set to skip the VIP entry into Chennai airport via Gate 6 and will enter through the regular T2 international terminal like other passengers to fly to London, after the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) denied entry to his advisor Vishnu Reddy, who is accompanying the CM on his maiden overseas visit to woo investments, citing security reasons.Airport sources said only the President and Prime Minister are eligible for ceremonial entry into the airport, while the facility is extended to the chief minister and governor of the particular state on special request.While the chief minister's office made a request for special entry for the chief minister on Thursday, BCAS accepted it but said that persons accompanying the VIP should enter through the regular international terminal as per protocol.However, the chief minister reportedly refused to use the VIP gate only for himself and decided to enter the airport like other international passengers.After receiving the information, airport authorities made arrangements to usher in the guests through Gate No. D9, which is used only for emergencies. A heavy posse of police personnel has also been deployed at Chennai airport to avoid crowding at the terminal.
Article Summary: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is set to skip the VIP entry into Chennai airport via Gate 6. He will enter through the regular T2 international terminal like other passengers to fly to London. The Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) denied entry to his advisor Vishnu Reddy, citing security reasons.

Article Title: Delhi man, 22, stabbed 17 times near school over suspected affair
Article Text:
A 22-year-old man died after being stabbed seventeen times in east Delhi's Mandawali area.





NEW DELHI: A 22-year-old man was stabbed 17 times and killed after an altercation with two men near a school in east Delhi’s Mandawali on Thursday evening, with police suspecting that the accused believed the victim was having an affair with his sister.A PCR call about the stabbing was received at 7:54pm, following which police reached near Gyan Vatika School and rushed the injured man, identified as Vansh Dedha, to Max Hospital. He was declared brought dead. Doctors found 17 stab injuries on his body.Preliminary inquiry revealed that Dedha had an altercation with Keshav Kumar, 22, a resident of Karawal Nagar, and his associate. Police suspect Kumar attacked Dedha after believing that he was having an affair with his sister. Kumar and his associate allegedly chased Dedha and repeatedly stabbed him with a sharp-edged weapon near the school before fleeing the spot.A murder case was registered at Mandawali police station and Kumar was arrested during the investigation. Police have also identified the second accused and are conducting raids to apprehend him.The knife allegedly used in the murder and the clothes worn during the incident have been recovered, while the motorcycle allegedly used by the accused has also been taken into police possession.CCTV footage from the area and technical surveillance are being examined to establish the sequence of events. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A 22-year-old man was stabbed 17 times and killed after an altercation with two men near a school in east Delhi’s Mandawali on Thursday evening. Police suspect that the accused believed the victim was having an affair with his sister.

Article Title: ‘Enough is enough’: Bombay HC seeks names of ward officers responsible for garbage on streets
Article Text:
The Bombay High Court ordered the BMC to identify accountable officers for street garbage





MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Thursday directed the BMC to submit names of ward officers and officers on field responsible for maintaining hygiene and cleanliness, who can be held accountable for garbage dumped on public streets and open spaces.“Enough is enough. The moment we get a complaint, we’ll hold the particular officer responsible and ensure he is not there in public service,’’ said Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale while hearing a petition by Kannamwar Nagar CHS regarding odour from Kanjurmarg dumping ground.In recent hearings, HC flagged total non-compliance by BMC in clearing trash, waste, litter on public streets. The judges said “ward officers are not functioning properly.” Referring to a photograph, Justice Kulkarni told senior advocate Anil Sakhare, for BMC, “This is Dadar. We’ll provide you with entire Mumbai (photographs), if your commissioner is not aware about it.”The judges said it appears that BMC’s assurances “were paper assurances.” “There is no alternative but to direct the municipal commissioner to put the house in order and fix accountability” on officers who are not taking action to prevent dumping of waste on public streets.They directed an SOP to be placed at the next hearing.They also said BMC will have to strictly implement Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, that casts duties on urban local bodies. “We always want Bombay (sic) corporation to be a model corporation. It is not happening… Segregation is going to have more importance in the coming times…festival times. Otherwise it will be chaotic,’’ said Justice Kulkarni. The judges also said, “the problem is there is a mental block with all citizens” and “wherever there is open space, streets, they dump waste. ”They directed expeditious appointment of a task force for implementing the Rules. Citing the example of Singapore, which imposes heavy fines on offenders, they said the state govt must come out with a “uniform policy.”Adjourning the hearing to Oct 7, the judges said BMC must issue “public sensitive” advertisements in newspapers and TV and also encourage social influencers to give messages to citizens not to throw garbage on public streets. “A sense of belonging of citizens needs to be inculcated,’’ said Justice Gokhale.
Article Summary: HC flagged total non-compliance by BMC in clearing trash, waste, litter on public streets. Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said “ward officers are not functioning properly’ They also said BMC will have to strictly implement Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.

Article Title: Watch: RTC bus swerves to avoid wrong-way car, ploughs into petrol bunk
Article Text:
Image Credit: X





HYDERABAD: A bus driver’s attempt to avoid a car that allegedly entered a service road from the wrong direction resulted in an RTC bus crashing into a petrol bunk at Batasingaram in Abdullapurmet.No injuries were reported in the incident, a video of which has since gone viral on social media.According to Abdullapurmet police, a case was registered against the RTC bus driver based on a complaint lodged by the petrol bunk manager, alleging damage to two cars and a fixed installation on the premises.Police said two cars were waiting to refuel when the bus, travelling along the service road, suddenly veered into the petrol bunk and collided with the vehicles and an installation. Bunk employees ran to safety after noticing the bus approaching at high speed. The bus eventually came to a halt inside the premises.However, an examination of CCTV footage revealed that a parked truck on the service road and a car that allegedly entered from the wrong direction contributed to the incident. Police said the bus driver’s view was obstructed by the parked truck, and he swerved left to avoid colliding with the car that suddenly appeared in front of him.Despite the evasive manoeuvre, the bus entered the petrol bunk and damaged two cars before coming to a stop. Police are investigating the incident.
Article Summary: An RTC bus crashed into a petrol bunk at Batasingaram in Abdullapurmet. No injuries were reported in the incident, a video of which has since gone viral on social media. A case has been registered against the bus driver. Police are investigating the incident.

Article Title: 20 coded messages of Akbar, Noor Jahan & Shah Jahan surface in Madhya Pradesh's Datia
Article Text:
Twenty cryptic Persian messages surfaced in Datia, Madhya Pradesh.





BHOPAL: Akbar sends a blessing. Noor Jahan offers reassurance. Shah Jahan pines for a beloved. Their words travel not by horse or herald, but by pigeon — tucked into tiny tubes tied to birds’ legs, more than three centuries ago.Twenty cryptic Persian messages, each barely four square inches, have surfaced in a private collection in Madhya Pradesh’s Datia, close to the UP border about 360 km north of Bhopal. No names. No signatures. Just symbols, texts and clues to a secretive Mughal world.The messages were found in Datia resident Radha Vallabh Mishra’s collection during a recent Gyan Bharatam Mission survey by archaeologist Wasim Khan, associated with the state directorate of archaeology, archives and museums. Some are believed to have been sent directly by Akbar, Noor Jahan and Shah Jahan.Mishra, who has collected old books and rare objects for more than five decades, acquired them about 40 years ago from an antique seller in Agra for around Rs 200. He began connecting them to the Mughal period from their paper, motifs, symbols, the name “Chandra Bhan” and Hijri dates on some pages.Chandra Bhan, sometimes Chandra Bhan Brahman, was a Punjabi poet of Persian who served as secretary to Shah Jahan.Impressed by his Persian literature, calligraphy and poetry, the emperor entrusted him with maintaining his personal diary. His “Chahar Chaman” chronicles Shah Jahan’s rule.Written in coded Persian Ramz, messages were examined by Persian-language experts Noor Ishtiyaq of archaeology and museums directorate and Urdu poets Wajahat Shah and Latif Ahmad.Instead of royal names, they found three golden symbols — a square, candle and rose — associated with Akbar, Noor Jahan and Shah Jahan respectively. “These messages were placed inside tiny tubes tied to pigeons’ legs,” Khan said. Who received them remains a mystery.Pigeon post was no flight of fancy at Mughal court and the find dovetails with Abul Fazl’s “Ain-i-Akbari”, which records Akbar’s passion for pigeon-flying, or ishqbazi, and describes an aviary with more than 20,000 birds, including 500 select pigeons. It identifies Raṭh as a pigeon trained chiefly to carry letters.One message attributed to Shah Jahan dwells on a beloved’s beauty, down to a tiny mole on her face, before turning wistful — a dream surviving in the heart despite changing times. Noor Jahan’s is intimate and reassuring: “The hour has arrived; there is no need to worry; happiness, fulfilment and refuge await.” Akbar’s reads like a blessing, invoking grace, generosity and greatness and imagining life as a garden blooming through countless springs.But experts said what reads like poetry may conceal something else. In Ramz, a rose may not be a rose, and a blessing may carry a message hidden in plain sight. “Cryptography and communication have been a historic need. These letters are the evidence of our evolution,” said archaeology commissioner Madan Kumar Nagargoje. Four centuries later, pigeons are long gone. Their secrets have just landed.
Article Summary: Twenty cryptic Persian messages surfaced in Datia, Madhya Pradesh. Some are believed to have been sent directly by Akbar, Noor Jahan and Shah Jahan. The messages were placed inside tiny tubes tied to pigeons’ legs.
